entries.german:
329. 1221 ianuarii 18 Laterani. Honorius III ordinem Theutonicum sub apostolicae sedis protectione iubet esse conceditque, ut undique clericos su- scipiat et liberae sepulturae privilegio fruatur.

Honorius episcopus servus servorum dei magistro et fratribus hospitalis sancte Marie Theutonicorum Ierosolimitani salutem et apostolicam bene- dictionem. Quociens a nobis petitur, quod religioni et honestati convenire dinoscitur, animo nos decet libenti concedere et petencium desideriis congruum suffragium impertiri. Eapropter, dilecti in domino filii, vestris iustis postu lationibus clementer annuimus et domum vestram, in qua estis ad dei laudem et gloriam et defensionem suorum fidelium et liberandam dei ecclesiam con- gregati, cum omnibus possessionibus et bonis suis, que inpresenciarum legitime habere cognoscitur aut in futurum concessione pontificum, liberalitate regum vel principum, oblatione fidelium seu aliis iustis modis prestante domino poterit adipisci tam trans mare quam cis mare, vobis auctoritate apostolica confirmamus et1 perpetuis futuris temporibus sub apostolice sedis tutela et protectione consistant. Ut autem vobis ad curam animarum vestrarum et sa- lutis plenitudinem nichil desit atque ecclesiastica sacramenta et divina officia vestro sacro collegio exhibeantur commodius, statuimus, ut liceat vobis ho- nestos clericos et sacerdotes secundum deum quantum ad vestram conscientiam ordinatos undecumque ad vos venientes suscipere et tam in principali domo vestra quam eciam in obedienciis et locis sibi subdictis vobiscum habere, dummodo, si e vicino sint, eos a propriis episcopis expetatis iidemque nulli alii professioni vel ordini teneantur obuoxii. Preterea nulli persone extra vestrum capitulum sint subiecti tibique, dilecte in domino fili magister, tuis- que successoribus tanquam magistro et prelato suo deferant secundum vestri ordinis instituta. Quicunque vero in cimiterio vestro elegerint sepeliri, ad se- pulturam recipiendi, educendi et sepeliendi, nisi forte excommunicati vel no- minatim fuerint interdicti aut eciam publice1 usurarii, facultatem liberam ha- beatis, salva tamen iusticia illarum ecclesiarum, a quibus mortuorum corpora assumuntur. Decernimus ergo, ut nulli omnino hominum liceat hanc paginam nostre confirmationis et constitutionis infringere vel ei ausu temerario contraire. Si quis autem hoc attemptare presumpserit, indignationem omnipotentis dei et beatorum Petri et Pauli apostolorum eius se noverit incursurum. Datum Laterani xv kal. februarii pontificatus nostri anno v. Sine d.ito: I, 71v.; 11,107 n. 59; A. 20 n. 57 Latine et Oermanice.— Cumdato: Laterani xv kal.-febr. p. n. a. 5. Originale cum bulla in archivo Regimontano; cf. Napiersky I, 4 n. 14. Apographum vidimationis factae per Bonacursum de ordine cet. et Gailardum cet. d. d. Accon 1277 oct. 19 e domo Ellingensi: R. 39. — Protectionis clausulam transsumsit Nicolaus Pomesa- niensis episcepus 1371 iunii 7 petente Swedero de Pelland o. T. thesaurario, Iohanne auondam Sonchen de Rosinberg et Iohanne Muench de Elbingo, notariis, subscribentibus. Originale cum episcopi sigillo in archivo Regimontano. 1. I. R. ut II. A. 20. 2. sic. Originale; alii: publici.
entries.english:
On 18 January 1221 at the Lateran, Honorius III orders that the Teutonic Order remain under the protection of the Apostolic See and grants it the right to receive clerics from anywhere and to enjoy the privilege of free burial.

Honorius, bishop and servant of the servants of God, to the master and brothers of the Hospital of Saint Mary of the Germans of Jerusalem, greeting and apostolic blessing. Since we ought willingly to grant what is recognized as fitting for religion and honesty, we approve your just petitions and confirm by apostolic authority your house, gathered for God's praise and the defense of his faithful and the liberation of the Church, with all its possessions and goods, present and future, acquired by lawful means, whether across or this side of the sea. They shall remain under the protection and guardianship of the Apostolic See forever. For the care of your souls, we establish that you may receive honest clerics and priests, properly ordained, from anywhere, and keep them with you in your principal house, obediences, and dependent places, provided that those from nearby are requested from their own bishops and are not bound to another profession or order. No person outside your chapter shall be subject to you; the master and his successors shall be honored as master and prelate according to the statutes of the Order. You may freely receive, remove, and bury in your cemetery those who choose burial there, except the excommunicated, those expressly under interdict, and public usurers, while preserving the rights of the churches from which the bodies are taken. No one may infringe this confirmation and constitution; whoever attempts it shall incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul. Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of February, in the fifth year of our pontificate.
